items.name: Legislative powers vested in Congress
items.summary: The legislative powers granted by the Constitution are vested in a Congress consisting of a Senate and a House.
items.qualifications: Vesting is limited to legislative powers herein granted, not a grant of a general police power.

items.name: House impeachment
items.summary: The House has the sole power of impeachment.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Senate impeachment trial
items.summary: The Senate has sole power to try all impeachments, subject to prescribed trial conditions.
items.qualifications: The Chief Justice presides when the President is tried; conviction requires two thirds of members present.

items.name: Revenue bills originate in House
items.summary: Bills for raising revenue originate in the House; the Senate may propose or concur with amendments.
items.qualifications: The Constitution's revenue-origination category is narrower than every measure with fiscal implications.

items.name: Presentment and veto
items.summary: Bills passed by both Houses are presented to the President and processed under constitutional approval, return, veto and override procedures.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Taxing authority
items.summary: Congress may lay and collect taxes, duties, imposts, and excises to pay debts and provide for common defense and general welfare.
items.qualifications: Taxing power is constitutionally constrained, including applicable uniformity and other restrictions; does not establish unlimited regulatory competence.

items.name: Spending for national purposes
items.summary: Congress may provide for federal debts, common defense, and the general welfare through authorized expenditures.
items.qualifications: Modern Spending Clause doctrine and limitations require separate case-law evidence.

items.name: Uniform duties, imposts and excises
items.summary: Duties, imposts, and excises must be uniform throughout the United States.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Borrow on United States credit
items.summary: Congress may borrow money on the credit of the United States.
items.qualifications: Power is subject to the text, amendments, and controlling judicial construction.

items.name: Regulate specified commerce
items.summary: Congress may regulate commerce with foreign nations, among the states, and with Indian tribes.
items.qualifications: Power is subject to the text, amendments, and controlling judicial construction.

items.name: Establish uniform naturalization and bankruptcy laws
items.summary: Congress may establish a uniform rule of naturalization and uniform bankruptcy laws throughout the United States.
items.qualifications: Power is subject to the text, amendments, and controlling judicial construction.

items.name: Coinage and weights and measures
items.summary: Congress may coin money, regulate the value of domestic and foreign coin, and fix the standard of weights and measures.
items.qualifications: Power is subject to the text, amendments, and controlling judicial construction.

items.name: Punish counterfeiting
items.summary: Congress may provide for punishment for counterfeiting securities and current coin of the United States.
items.qualifications: Power is subject to the text, amendments, and controlling judicial construction.

items.name: Establish postal facilities
items.summary: Congress may establish post offices and post roads.
items.qualifications: Power is subject to the text, amendments, and controlling judicial construction.

items.name: Protect limited author and inventor exclusivity
items.summary: Congress may secure limited-time exclusive rights to authors and inventors for their writings and discoveries to promote progress.
items.qualifications: Power is subject to the text, amendments, and controlling judicial construction.

items.name: Constitute inferior federal tribunals
items.summary: Congress may constitute tribunals inferior to the Supreme Court.
items.qualifications: Power is subject to the text, amendments, and controlling judicial construction.

items.name: Define and punish piracy and law-of-nations offenses
items.summary: Congress may define and punish high-seas piracies and felonies, and offenses against the law of nations.
items.qualifications: Power is subject to the text, amendments, and controlling judicial construction.

items.name: Declare war and regulate captures
items.summary: Congress may declare war, grant letters of marque and reprisal, and make rules on captures.
items.qualifications: Power is subject to the text, amendments, and controlling judicial construction.

items.name: Raise and support armies
items.summary: Congress may raise and support armies, with specific restrictions on appropriations.
items.qualifications: No appropriation of money to that use shall be for a longer term than two years.

items.name: Provide and maintain a navy
items.summary: Congress may provide and maintain a navy.
items.qualifications: Power is subject to the text, amendments, and controlling judicial construction.

items.name: Regulate land and naval forces
items.summary: Congress may make rules governing and regulating the land and naval forces.
items.qualifications: Power is subject to the text, amendments, and controlling judicial construction.

items.name: Call forth militia for enumerated purposes
items.summary: Congress may provide for calling forth militia to execute federal laws, suppress insurrections, and repel invasions.
items.qualifications: Power is subject to the text, amendments, and controlling judicial construction.

items.name: Organize and discipline militia
items.summary: Congress may provide for organizing, arming and disciplining militia and governing those employed in federal service, with reserved state appointments and training authority.
items.qualifications: Appointment of militia officers and training according to congressional discipline are reserved to the states.

items.name: Legislate for federal district and enclaves
items.summary: Congress may exercise exclusive legislation in constitutionally described federal districts and acquired enclaves.
items.qualifications: Power is subject to the text, amendments, and controlling judicial construction.

items.name: Enact necessary and proper implementing laws
items.summary: Congress may make laws necessary and proper for carrying into execution constitutionally vested federal powers.
items.qualifications: A means-of-execution power tethered to constitutionally vested powers; no freestanding unlimited police power.

items.name: Army appropriation period limit
items.summary: Appropriations of money to raise and support armies may not run for longer than two years.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Habeas suspension restrictions
items.summary: The privilege of the writ of habeas corpus shall not be suspended except under the Constitution's rebellion-or-invasion and public-safety conditions.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Federal bills of attainder and ex post facto laws
items.summary: The Constitution prohibits federal bills of attainder and ex post facto laws.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Federal export duties prohibited
items.summary: No federal tax or duty shall be laid on articles exported from any state.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Appropriation by law required
items.summary: Treasury money can be drawn only in consequence of appropriations made by law, with public statements and accounts of receipts and expenditures.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Federal titles of nobility and restricted foreign emoluments
items.summary: No federal title of nobility may be granted; acceptance of specified foreign benefits by covered officeholders requires congressional consent.
items.qualifications: Foreign emoluments restrictions have defined persons and consent conditions; do not treat as applying identically to all private citizens.

items.name: Restrictions on states making treaties and coining money
items.summary: Article I Section 10 forbids states from exercising specified foreign affairs, monetary and similar powers.
items.qualifications: Specific prohibitions differ by subject and should be further decomposed in subsequent increments.

items.name: State import/export duties constrained
items.summary: States face constitutional limits on imposts and duties on imports or exports, subject to enumerated exceptions and congressional consent.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: State war and compact restrictions
items.summary: States may not exercise specified war, troop and interstate-compact powers outside constitutional exceptions and congressional consent.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Executive power vested in President
items.summary: The executive power is vested in the President of the United States.
items.qualifications: Do not infer that the President may disregard statutes or constitutional protections, or that all independent agencies lack statutory independence.

items.name: States appoint electors
items.summary: Each state appoints presidential electors in the manner directed by its legislature, subject to other constitutional provisions and valid federal law.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Presidential eligibility conditions
items.summary: The President must satisfy the citizenship, age and residency qualifications established in Article II.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Commander in Chief
items.summary: The President is Commander in Chief of the armed forces and militia when called into federal service.
items.qualifications: Does not itself settle war-initiation, spending, domestic policing, or force-employment questions; Congress has express war and military powers.

items.name: Pardons and reprieves
items.summary: The President may grant reprieves and pardons for offenses against the United States, except in cases of impeachment.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Require written opinions from department heads
items.summary: The President may require written opinions from principal officers of executive departments on their respective duties.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Treaty-making with Senate consent
items.summary: The President may make treaties with advice and consent of the Senate, provided two thirds of Senators present concur.
items.qualifications: Do not confuse treaty ratification with congressional implementation legislation or executive agreements.

items.name: Nomination and appointment with Senate consent
items.summary: The President nominates and, with Senate advice and consent, appoints specified principal officers; Congress may vest appointments of inferior officers in specified actors by law.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Temporary appointments during Senate recess
items.summary: The President may fill certain vacancies during a Senate recess through temporary commissions under constitutional conditions.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Faithful execution of laws
items.summary: The President must take care that the laws be faithfully executed.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: State of the Union information
items.summary: The President shall from time to time provide Congress information on the state of the Union and recommend measures considered necessary and expedient.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Impeachment and removal from federal civil office
items.summary: The President, Vice President and all civil officers of the United States are removed upon impeachment for and conviction of specified offenses.
items.qualifications: The text sets constitutional impeachment and conviction conditions; this is not a universal criminal-penalty rule.

items.name: Judicial power vested in federal courts
items.summary: Judicial power is vested in one Supreme Court and inferior federal courts Congress may establish.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Article III judicial tenure and compensation
items.summary: Article III judges hold office during good behavior, with compensation protections during continuance in office.
items.qualifications: Applies to Article III judicial offices; does not silently extend identical tenure to every Article I tribunal.

items.name: Federal cases and controversies
items.summary: Article III describes categories of cases and controversies within the federal judicial power.
items.qualifications: Subject to constitutional amendments, jurisdictional statutes, sovereign immunity doctrine and justiciability requirements.

items.name: Supreme Court original and appellate jurisdiction
items.summary: Article III distinguishes Supreme Court original jurisdiction from appellate jurisdiction, with constitutionally defined congressional exceptions and regulations.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Jury trial of crimes
items.summary: Article III protects jury trial in covered criminal cases except impeachment, with prescribed place of trial.
items.qualifications: Specific criminal jury guarantees and their scope also appear in the Sixth Amendment.

items.name: Definition and proof of treason
items.summary: Treason has a defined constitutional scope and unusually stringent evidentiary or confession requirements.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Full faith and credit between states
items.summary: States must give constitutionally required full faith and credit to other states' public acts, records and judicial proceedings.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Privileges and immunities of interstate citizenship
items.summary: Article IV protects privileges and immunities of citizens in the several states.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Interstate extradition
items.summary: Article IV establishes an interstate process for returning persons charged with certain crimes and found in another state.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Admit new states
items.summary: Congress may admit new states subject to consent conditions for dividing or joining existing states.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Rules for federal territories and property
items.summary: Congress may dispose of and make needful rules and regulations concerning U.S. territory and other federal property.
items.qualifications: This is not a general assertion of exclusive federal authority over every nonfederal local matter.

items.name: Republican government and federal protection of states
items.summary: The United States guarantees states a republican form of government and protection against invasion, and provides conditional protection against domestic violence.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Constitutional amendment proposal routes
items.summary: Amendments may be proposed by two thirds of both Houses or a convention called upon application of two thirds of state legislatures.
items.qualifications: A convention-call requirement is conditional on the constitutionally specified applications.

items.name: Constitutional amendment ratification routes
items.summary: Proposed amendments become part of the Constitution upon ratification by three fourths of states using the mode selected under Article V.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Equal suffrage of states in Senate protected
items.summary: No state may be deprived of its equal suffrage in the Senate without its consent.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Supremacy of Constitution and valid federal law
items.summary: The Constitution, federal laws made in pursuance of it, and treaties made under U.S. authority constitute supreme law, binding state judges despite conflicting state law.
items.qualifications: Only constitutionally valid federal law enjoys supremacy; the clause grants no freestanding legislative power.

items.name: Constitutional oath required
items.summary: Specified federal and state officers must be bound by oath or affirmation to support the Constitution.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: No religious test for federal public office
items.summary: No religious test may be required as a qualification for any office or public trust under the United States.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Religious liberty and non-establishment
items.summary: The First Amendment limits laws respecting establishment of religion or prohibiting free exercise.
items.qualifications: The text refers to Congress; modern application to states and other government conduct depends on separately modeled constitutional doctrine.

items.name: Freedom of speech and press
items.summary: The First Amendment protects speech and press against covered governmental restrictions.
items.qualifications: Not an absolute prohibition on every law affecting expression; doctrinal tests and incorporation require separate treatment.

items.name: Peaceful assembly and petition
items.summary: The First Amendment protects peaceful assembly and petition for redress of grievances.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Right to keep and bear arms
items.summary: The Second Amendment protects the right of the people to keep and bear arms.
items.qualifications: Scope, public-safety regulations, and state application require judicial doctrine; avoid treating the right as unconditional.

items.name: Quartering-of-soldiers restriction
items.summary: The Third Amendment restricts quartering soldiers in houses, subject to peace/war distinctions and law.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Searches and seizures
items.summary: The Fourth Amendment protects the people against unreasonable searches and seizures and regulates warrants.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Grand jury and double-jeopardy protections
items.summary: The Fifth Amendment contains federal criminal-procedure protections for covered prosecutions.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Self-incrimination protection
items.summary: The Fifth Amendment protects against compelled self-incrimination in criminal cases.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Fifth Amendment due process
items.summary: The Fifth Amendment forbids deprivation of life, liberty or property without due process of law.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Just compensation for public takings
items.summary: Private property may not be taken for public use without just compensation.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Criminal-trial safeguards
items.summary: The Sixth Amendment protects specified speedy/public trial, jury, notice, confrontation, compulsory process and counsel rights.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Civil jury trial protection
items.summary: The Seventh Amendment preserves jury trial in qualifying suits at common law above the textual threshold.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Excessive bail, excessive fines and cruel punishments
items.summary: The Eighth Amendment prohibits excessive bail and fines and cruel and unusual punishments.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Enumeration does not deny other retained rights
items.summary: The Ninth Amendment says enumeration of constitutional rights shall not be construed to deny or disparage others retained by the people.
items.qualifications: Does not by itself identify the contents of any particular unenumerated right.

items.name: Reserved powers
items.summary: Powers not delegated to the United States nor prohibited to the states are reserved to the states respectively or to the people.
items.qualifications: Does not negate powers otherwise validly delegated to the United States.

items.name: Eleventh Amendment jurisdictional restriction
items.summary: The Eleventh Amendment limits construction of federal judicial power over specified suits against a state by citizens of another state or foreign citizens or subjects.
items.qualifications: The full state-sovereign-immunity doctrine is broader and requires separate case-law sources.

items.name: Separate electoral ballots and contingent presidential election
items.summary: The Twelfth Amendment prescribes separate presidential and vice-presidential electoral votes and specified contingent elections.
items.qualifications: A historical presidential transition portion of the original amendment text was superseded by the Twentieth Amendment.

items.name: Abolition of slavery and involuntary servitude
items.summary: The Thirteenth Amendment prohibits slavery and involuntary servitude, with an express exception for punishment for crime after due conviction.
items.qualifications: The Thirteenth Amendment directly prohibits slavery and involuntary servitude by public or private actors, subject to the textual exception for duly convicted crime punishment. Do not presume that every form of compelled work falls within that exception.

items.name: Congressional enforcement of Thirteenth Amendment
items.summary: Congress may enforce the Thirteenth Amendment through appropriate legislation.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Fourteenth Amendment citizenship
items.summary: The Fourteenth Amendment defines U.S. and state citizenship for persons born or naturalized in the United States and subject to its jurisdiction.
items.qualifications: Do not convert textual citizenship language into unsupported conclusions about disputed citizenship applications.

items.name: Privileges or immunities of United States citizenship
items.summary: States may not make or enforce laws abridging privileges or immunities of citizens of the United States under the Fourteenth Amendment.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Fourteenth Amendment due process
items.summary: States may not deprive any person of life, liberty, or property without due process of law.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Equal protection of the laws
items.summary: States may not deny any person within their jurisdiction equal protection of the laws.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Fourteenth Amendment insurrection disqualification
items.summary: Section 3 specifies public-office disqualification for certain oath-taking persons engaged in insurrection or rebellion and a congressional removal mechanism.
items.qualifications: Procedures, scope, and enforcement actors require review of controlling case law; no self-executing implementation is asserted.

items.name: Congressional enforcement of Fourteenth Amendment
items.summary: Congress may enforce the Fourteenth Amendment through appropriate legislation.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Voting restrictions based on race
items.summary: Voting rights of U.S. citizens shall not be denied or abridged by the United States or states because of race, color, or previous condition of servitude.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Congressional enforcement of Fifteenth Amendment
items.summary: Congress may enforce the Fifteenth Amendment through appropriate legislation.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Income taxation without apportionment
items.summary: Congress may lay and collect income taxes without apportionment among states or regard to a census or enumeration.
items.qualifications: This does not erase every other constitutional restriction on federal taxation.

items.name: Popular election of senators
items.summary: The Seventeenth Amendment replaces state-legislature selection of Senators with popular election and specifies vacancies and temporary appointments.
items.qualifications: State legislatures may enable temporary gubernatorial appointments under constitutional conditions.

items.name: Prohibition historically established and repealed
items.summary: The Eighteenth Amendment once established beverage alcohol prohibition and concurrent enforcement powers; it was repealed by the Twenty-First Amendment.
items.qualifications: Historical record only. Must not be treated as a currently operative restriction or power.

items.name: Voting restrictions based on sex
items.summary: Citizens' voting rights shall not be denied or abridged by the United States or states because of sex.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Federal office terms and congressional convening
items.summary: The Twentieth Amendment changes dates for federal presidential/congressional terms and congressional annual convening.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Presidential transition contingencies
items.summary: The Twentieth Amendment provides rules for president-elect death, failure to qualify and related contingencies.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Eighteenth Amendment repealed
items.summary: The Twenty-First Amendment repeals the Eighteenth Amendment.
items.qualifications: Repeal is operative; prohibition is not reinstated by recording it in the historical register.

items.name: Alcohol importation violating state law
items.summary: The Twenty-First Amendment prohibits transporting or importing intoxicating liquor into a state or covered territory for delivery or use in violation of its law.
items.qualifications: Interpretation alongside Commerce Clause and other constitutional rules must be modeled separately.

items.name: Presidential election term limits
items.summary: The Twenty-Second Amendment limits how many times a person may be elected President, including specified succession scenarios.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: District of Columbia presidential electors
items.summary: The Twenty-Third Amendment establishes presidential electors for the District of Columbia under specified population and congressional constraints.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Poll-tax restrictions in federal elections
items.summary: The Twenty-Fourth Amendment prohibits denying or abridging citizen voting rights in specified federal elections for failure to pay a poll tax or other tax.
items.qualifications: Text specifically addresses federal elections; state-election protections may involve separate judicial doctrine.

items.name: Presidential succession and disability
items.summary: The Twenty-Fifth Amendment establishes mechanisms for succession, vice-presidential vacancies, voluntary inability, and contested inability.
items.qualifications: Sections set distinct triggering actors, written notices, deadlines and voting thresholds; do not collapse them into an unrestricted removal authority.

items.name: Voting restrictions based on age eighteen and older
items.summary: Voting rights of U.S. citizens aged eighteen or older may not be denied or abridged by the United States or states on account of age.
items.qualifications: Does not eliminate other lawful voter qualifications.

items.name: Congressional enforcement of Twenty-Sixth Amendment
items.summary: Congress may enforce the Twenty-Sixth Amendment through appropriate legislation.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Congressional compensation timing
items.summary: A law varying congressional compensation cannot take effect until an election of Representatives has intervened.
items.qualifications: Scope subject to constitutional text, controlling amendments, and applicable judicial precedent.

items.name: Original presidential ballot provisions superseded
items.summary: Original Article II presidential elector voting provisions have been superseded by the Twelfth Amendment.
items.qualifications: Historical-only legal change record; no operative procedure may bind to it.

items.name: Original Senator selection method superseded
items.summary: The original state-legislature selection of U.S. Senators was superseded by the Seventeenth Amendment.
items.qualifications: Historical-only; current selection governed by the Seventeenth Amendment.

items.name: Original fugitive-service provision superseded
items.summary: The original Article IV fugitive-service provision was rendered inoperative by the Thirteenth Amendment.
items.qualifications: Historical-only provision; cannot be asserted as a present enforceable obligation.

items.name: Biennial House elections
items.summary: Members of the House are chosen every second year by the people of the states.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: House electorate qualification reference
items.summary: State House-election electors must possess the qualifications required for electors of the state's most numerous legislative branch.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: House membership eligibility
items.summary: Representatives must be at least 25, citizens for seven years, and inhabitants of the electing state when elected.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: House apportionment and decennial enumeration
items.summary: Apportionment includes an enumeration within ten-year intervals and at least one Representative for each state; original population formula was modified by later amendments.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Superseded three-fifths population formula
items.summary: Original apportionment included a three-fifths formula made inoperative by subsequent constitutional change.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: House vacancy election writ
items.summary: The executive authority of a state must issue writs of election to fill a House vacancy.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: House selection of Speaker and officers
items.summary: The House chooses its Speaker and other officers.
items.qualifications: Constitutionally specified actor and subject; further statutory implementation and judicial interpretation remain distinct.

items.name: Two Senators per state and equal voting
items.summary: The Senate comprises two Senators per state serving six-year terms with one vote each; original selection method was replaced.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Senate staggered classes
items.summary: Senate seats are arranged in three classes so that approximately one third of seats are contested every second year.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Senate membership eligibility
items.summary: Senators must be at least 30 years old, citizens for nine years, and inhabitants of their state when elected.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Vice President Senate presidency and tie vote
items.summary: The Vice President is President of the Senate but may vote only when the Senate is equally divided.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Senate choice of officers and president pro tempore
items.summary: The Senate chooses its officers and a president pro tempore when the Vice President is absent or exercises the Presidency.
items.qualifications: Constitutionally specified actor and subject; further statutory implementation and judicial interpretation remain distinct.

items.name: Senate impeachment trial procedures
items.summary: Senate impeachment trials require oath or affirmation, Chief Justice presidency for trials of the President, and two-thirds concurrence of members present for conviction.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Limited impeachment judgment
items.summary: Impeachment judgment can extend only to removal and disqualification; a convicted party remains subject to separate lawful criminal process.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: State regulation of congressional elections
items.summary: State legislatures prescribe congressional-election time, place and manner subject to Congress's constitutionally provided power to alter.
items.qualifications: Constitutionally specified actor and subject; further statutory implementation and judicial interpretation remain distinct.

items.name: Congressional alteration of election rules
items.summary: Congress may by law make or alter constitutionally specified state regulations for congressional elections.
items.qualifications: Constitutionally specified actor and subject; further statutory implementation and judicial interpretation remain distinct.

items.name: Annual congressional assembly
items.summary: Congress must assemble at least once each year; the default meeting date was later changed by the Twentieth Amendment.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Each House judges elections and qualifications
items.summary: Each chamber judges the election, returns and qualifications of its own members.
items.qualifications: Constitutionally specified actor and subject; further statutory implementation and judicial interpretation remain distinct.

items.name: Chamber quorum and minority attendance procedures
items.summary: A majority of each chamber constitutes a business quorum; a smaller number may adjourn daily and compel absent members under its rules.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Each House determines internal rules
items.summary: Each chamber determines the rules of its proceedings and may discipline members for disorderly behavior.
items.qualifications: Constitutionally specified actor and subject; further statutory implementation and judicial interpretation remain distinct.

items.name: Member expulsion with two-thirds concurrence
items.summary: Each chamber may expel a member with the concurrence of two-thirds of its members.
items.qualifications: Constitutionally specified actor and subject; further statutory implementation and judicial interpretation remain distinct.

items.name: Chamber journal publication and recorded votes
items.summary: Each chamber keeps a journal, publishes its proceedings subject to a secrecy exception, and enters yeas and nays on demand of one-fifth of those present.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Inter-chamber consent to lengthy adjournment
items.summary: Neither chamber may adjourn beyond three days or change session place without the other's consent while Congress is in session.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Legislative compensation fixed by law
items.summary: Senators and Representatives receive compensation determined by law and paid from the Treasury, subject to the Twenty-Seventh Amendment's timing rule.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Arrest privilege during legislative travel and attendance
items.summary: Members are privileged from arrest during attendance and travel, subject to constitutional enumerated exceptions.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Speech or Debate protection for legislative activity
items.summary: For speech or debate in either chamber, members may not be questioned elsewhere.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Term-based ineligibility for created or enriched civil offices
items.summary: A member may not during the elected term be appointed to a civil office established or with emoluments increased during that term.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Simultaneous service in Congress and federal office
items.summary: A person holding an office under the United States may not simultaneously be a member of either chamber.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Presentment of legislative orders and resolutions
items.summary: Qualifying concurrent orders, resolutions or votes receive presidential presentment; questions of adjournment are expressly excepted.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Uniform naturalization and bankruptcy
items.summary: Naturalization rules and bankruptcy laws under this power must be uniform.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Time-limited authors' and inventors' rights
items.summary: The exclusive rights provided under the Intellectual Property Clause must be limited in time and tied to the enumerated subject matter and purpose.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Expired pre-1808 importation prohibition
items.summary: The original Article I § 9 restriction on forbidding specified migration/importation expired by its own date; it is historical rather than current authority.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Direct-tax apportionment subject to Sixteenth Amendment
items.summary: Direct taxes are subject to apportionment except that the Sixteenth Amendment permits income taxation without apportionment.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: No preferences for state ports
items.summary: Federal commerce and revenue regulation may not prefer ports of one state or compel specified clearances and duty payments in another state.
items.qualifications: Textual summary only; amendment qualifications and controlling doctrine must be evaluated separately.

items.name: Congressional consent to certain foreign gifts and benefits
items.summary: Congress may consent to covered federal officeholders accepting specified presents, emoluments, offices or titles from foreign sovereigns.
items.qualifications: Constitutionally specified actor and subject; further statutory implementation and judicial interpretation remain distinct.

items.name: Congressional consent to state import/export duties
items.summary: Congress may consent to specified state import/export duties, subject to clause-specific inspection, accounting and federal revision rules.
items.qualifications: Constitutionally specified actor and subject; further statutory implementation and judicial interpretation remain distinct.

items.name: Congressional consent to state tonnage duties and compacts
items.summary: Congress may give consent where Article I § 10 requires it for state tonnage duties, military arrangements or interstate/international compacts.
items.qualifications: Constitutionally specified actor and subject; further statutory implementation and judicial interpretation remain distinct.
